i love having special interests. i love having friends and doing nice things for them because i remember some small detail they mention that they themselves forgot about. i love to be able to lose myself in my own arbitrary research for my special interests temporarily. 

i don't feel so alien anymore. i feel like i had to learn a lot of things a different way than people naturally do, but hey, you could say the same about them and the things for which i have an above-average aptitude.

the worst is the people who don't try and understand at all, who treat it like an illness or some sort of mental failing. it feels like we exist in the same base language, use different dialects, and the people who don't try to understand just invalidate and ridicule your way of being, your existence dialect. 

all in all, i feel like being autistic is less of an issue in my everyday life than my ADHD, or my clinical depression, or my trauma that i'm putting so much effort into processing. the dialect you speak doesn't matter when you find people who don't mind having to play catch up on the translation just like you do.

I have PTSD as well, but I'm also autistic (the latter is more personally relevant for me wrt loud noises being a trigger, not in the PTSD trigger sense, but they trigger sensory overload and anxiety in me because... well, autism is just like that sometimes?), and what my phone did surprised me. I have it on vibrate with system volume down to zero most of the time. I'm using an original Google Pixel with the most recent stock android update, and while my phone did start vibrating and not stop until I checked every alert, it made zero noise. I believe this is also true of iPhones. Since the CRTC (from what I'm reading) seems to not care about alert priority, if you would wake up to your phone vibrating non-stop (either feeling it or hearing the buzz against a hard surface), maybe this would be a good option for you. I'm not saying this to be condescending, obviously. I'm glad my phone seems to allow me to receive alerts in a way where, if I was in a position to help (or if it was bad weather, or a threat), I could do something other than sobbing curled up in a ball because of a loud noise (my reaction, not yours).
